stem.text: A stationary sound wave is formed in a gas-filled tube of length $L$, which is closed at one end by a piston. The length of the tube can be altered by moving the piston.
The length of the tube and the frequency of the sound are varied so that the stationary wave always has two antinodes and two nodes, as shown.

stem.alt: Diagram of a gas-filled tube closed at one end by a piston, with a stationary wave drawn inside the tube; the length L is marked from the closed end to the piston, and a double-headed arrow shows the piston movement.

stem.text: The graph shows the variation of the frequency $f$ of the stationary sound wave with the length $L$ of the tube.

stem.alt: Graph of f/Hz against L/cm, with the vertical axis labelled f/Hz (0 to 5000) and the horizontal axis labelled L/cm (0 to 25); a curve falls steeply from the top of the vertical axis and then flattens as L increases.

stem.text: What is the speed of sound in the gas in the tube?
